newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slaughter brings "unequalled terror" to Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Slaughter brings "unequalled terror" to Algeria.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels killed up to 59 people in more massacres in hamlets near Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Saturday, just hours after President Liamine Zeroual spoke of "unequalled terror" in the country.
Algeria's main independent dailies all reported continued killings in the five-year-old conflict, and Le Matin said more than 250 people had now been killed in the past two weeks.

"Fifty-nine have been assassinated during this weekend in the centre of the country, mostly in Berroughia and in douars (villages) of Benramdane, Saouala and Baraki (near Algiers)," said Le Matin quoting villagers.

Zeroual vowed in a 20-minute televised address on Friday night to wipe out "criminals, traitors and mercenaries" -- Algeria's terms for Moslem fundamentalists. He said they were manipulated by unnamed foreign circles.

Without giving details of the slaughter, or any new steps to stop it, the president said: "...innocent citizens, of all categories, are victims each day of a blind terrorism never equalled in other times or other places."

More than 400 people have been killed since November. At least five bombs have exploded in Algiers and 17 been defused. Others have hit nearby towns. Hundreds of people have been maimed, caught as they shopped with their families.
In isolated communities, the chilling slaughter has continued. Whole families including infants have had their throats slit, their bodies mutilated.

Guerrillas killed 23 people by cutting their throats on Wednesday in Oumaria in Berrouaghia, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers, said Le Matin, without elaborating. These were in addition to the Thursday-Friday killings, it said.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed sources, said the four massacres were carried by rebels from Algeria's ruthless Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
The GIA had promised to increase killings during Ramadan.

Liberte newspaper, which reported two massacres, said about 50 Moslem guerrillas stormed the village of Houach el Hadj, some 40 km (25 miles) south of Algiers, and hacked to death 15 villagers about 30 minutes before Friday prayer.
The guerrillas killed 19 people, including 10 women and a two-year-old baby, by using axes and machetes in the neighbouring village of Benramdane, said Liberte.
Zeroual vowed on Friday his country would battle to the "final eradication of terrorism" which he said was being manipulated by foreigners bent on destabilising the North African country.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by radical Islamists.
The president promised that Algeria would pursue its path to democracy, but set no date for a fresh general election promised for the first half of this year.
His speech brought a disappointed reaction from many.
A commentator on Algerian state radio said: "Each important event coincides with a flare-up of violence coupled with political manoeuvres aimed at bringing chaos to the country."
She added: "This black series of violence in Ramadan is the worst and coincides with the great political deadline of elections this year."
